Research · payment networks · what partners get

Twenty-five networks, read as a partner would

What the card and ATM networks sell to issuers, acquirers, merchants, ATM operators, fintechs and developers, how each one lets a partner in, what its portals are like to use, and what partners say about them. Everything here is public and dated, and every sentence traces to its source.

25 networks · 33 browser walks · 3,756 ledger sources · 217 public demonstrations catalogued · read September 25, 2026

Networks25Six global, eleven US debit and ATM, eight international
Properties walked33Logged out, one scripted walk each, then read by hand
Ledger sources3,756Each with a quote, a URL and a date
Primary documents68%The rest is trade press and the networks' own claims

Scope

Partners only. Cardholder portals, apps and complaints are out of scope. Nothing behind a login was used for any network, Discover included, and no account was created on any site.

How to read the labels

Verified means read on a primary document: the network's own docs, rules, fee schedules or filings, a regulator, a court, or the browser on the day. Reported means trade press, analysts, forums and third-party demonstrations. Vendor means a network's claim about itself with no outside check. Hover a citation for its label and date.

The short version

  1. The front doors split into platforms and gateways. Visa, Mastercard, American Express, AP+, Elo and UnionPay put the catalogue and the sign-up on the public side, and most put the documentation there too (Visa Developer Center, Browse Products · Mastercard Developers · American Express Developers product catalogue · AP+ Developers, walked · ELO, walked · UnionPay International, Open Platform User Account Guide). Visa still holds SDKs and sample code behind sign-in, American Express locks some API references, and AP+ gates its documentation pages (Visa Developer Quick Start · American Express, High-Level Process · Australian Payments Plus Developers). Discover's Developer Center, JCB Partner Online, EASI and the PULSE client website ask the reader to identify themselves before showing any technical documentation (Visa Developer Center, walked · Mastercard Developers, walked · Discover Developer Center, walked). Discover is the only one of the four global card networks whose developer centre opens no documentation to a stranger (Discover Developer Center · DFS Services, Access denied). Its Explore page still names seven APIs, and its Partner Product Portal publishes OpenAPI specifications for twelve products (Discover Global Network, Explore APIs · Discover Partner Product Portal · Discover Partner Product Portal).
  2. An account buys most sandboxes at Visa and Mastercard, and production waits on a contract or an approval. Visa issues certification and production credentials only after a signed agreement, and Mastercard mints production credentials inactive until it approves (Pricing on Visa Developer · Mastercard Developers, Quick Start Guide · Visa, Going Live). American Express reviews each access request by hand, sandbox included, and Discover admits developers only through a representative (American Express Developers · American Express, Getting Started · developer.discover.com, FAQs). Visa's acceptance consoles come with default sandbox credentials (Visa Acceptance API Documentation · Authorize.net API Documentation). No sandbox in this study replays production data, and test cards are public only on the acquiring side (Visa Developer Quick Start · Mastercard Developers, BIN Lookup · Visa Acceptance Developer Portal, Testing Guide).
  3. Interchange is often public, and what the network itself charges almost never is. Visa, Mastercard, Interac, eftpos and Cartes Bancaires publish interchange schedules (Visa USA Interchange Reimbursement Fees · Mastercard 2026-2027 U.S. Region Interchange Programs · Interac, Understanding Fees · Australian Payments Plus, Interchange fees · Cartes Bancaires, Les commissions interchange). Only Interac publishes its switch fee to the tenth of a cent, and the card networks publish their own assessments for Canada alone (Interac, Understanding Fees · Visa Canada Standard Acquiring Network Assessment Fees · American Express, Network Assessment Fees · Discover Global Network, Standard Acquirer Rates). Canada's Code of Conduct requires that publication (Financial Consumer Agency of Canada, Code of Conduct for the Payment Card). Australia will require eftpos, Mastercard and Visa to publish quarterly aggregate scheme fee data from October 2026, and expects scheme fee roadmaps by April 2027 (Reserve Bank of Australia, Merchant Card Payment Costs and Surcharging · Reserve Bank of Australia, Scheme Fees · Reserve Bank of Australia, Transparency of Wholesale Fees · Reserve Bank of Australia, Impact and Implementation). The UK will require Visa and Mastercard to give acquirers clearer information on UK scheme and processing fees from July 2027 (Payment Systems Regulator, PS26/1: Market review of card scheme · Payment Systems Regulator, Specific direction 22).
  4. Visa, Mastercard, Elo and girocard publish their rules, and no US debit network does. The Visa rulebook runs to 923 pages, Mastercard's to four books, Elo's to 694 pages, and girocard publishes its admission contract (Visa Core Rules · Mastercard Rules for Merchants · Regulamento dos Arranjos de Pagamento ELO, Versão · Deutsche Kreditwirtschaft, Vertrag über die Zulassung als Netzbetreiber im). The American Express network manual, Discover's operating regulations and every PIN network's rules are confidential (American Express Global Network Policy · Discover 10-K 2024 · PULSE Network, Client Support · SHAZAM Payments Network). Mastercard announces rule changes inside Mastercard Connect, behind its sign-in (Mastercard, Chargebacks Made Simple Guide · Mastercard Connect, walked).
  5. The Discover family runs ten partner login pages, and no one account opens them. The Fraud and Risk Center, EASI, the Advanced Payments portal, eCentral, the Disputes Portal, the Release Compliance Tool, Web Merchant Boarding, the Developer Center, the Diners Club issuer site and the PULSE client website each have their own login (Discover Network Service Center · Discover Partner Product Portal · PULSE Network, Client Support). One Visa Partner account already opens Visa Developer and, after extra validation, Visa Online, which claims more than 150 services (Visa Partner Support and FAQ · Visa, Log). AP+ has folded three developer portals into one (Australian Payments Plus Developers).
  6. Mastercard and Visa's acquiring platform are the only ones that show API health in public. Its public status page reports each service for sandbox and production (Mastercard Developers, API Status). Visa runs a status page for its acquiring platform, sandbox included, and monthly release notes for its developer platform (Visa Acceptance Solutions Status · Visa, Release Notes). American Express's developer portal changelog stopped in May 2024, though its Payment Gateway keeps a versioned changelog (American Express, What's New · American Express, Gateway API Reference Documentation). No public Discover or PULSE site carries a status page or a changelog (Discover Partner Product Portal · PULSE Network, Insights & News).
  7. Ownership is moving under a third of the field. Capital One now owns Discover, PULSE and Diners Club and has moved its own debit cards onto them, more than doubling network volume in a year (Capital One Financial, Exhibit 99.1 · Capital One 10-Q 2026). Banks have explored buying STAR, and Fiserv has put its networks under review (Reuters, Google News RSS · Digital Transactions, The Past Will Not Be Prologue, Fiserv’s). Jeanie passed to Global Payments in January 2026, and CULIANCE is an FIS network, separate from the CO-OP network Velera still runs (Global Payments, Exhibit 99.1 · CULIANCE Network · Velera, CO-OP ATM Network).

Global card networks

Full profiles of the six networks with global card brands. Each opens with the finding that matters most to a partner, then the facts with their sources, how a partner gets in, what is sold, the portal as walked, what public video shows, and what partners say. The Discover family shares one walkthrough across its three brands.

Visa

Visa Inc. · San Francisco · VisaNet in more than 200 countries and territories · issuers, acquirers and processors, merchants, third-party agents, fintechs, technology partners, developers

Visa publishes the rulebook and hides the price. A member of the public can download Visa's rules, 923 redacted pages twice a year (Visa Core Rules). What the rulebook names but never prices is the rest: regional fee schedules that exist by title only, service fees that Principal clients pay in amounts the licensing page does not state, and developer pricing that is bespoke behind a contract (Visa Core Rules · Visa Licensing Program · Pricing on Visa Developer). A partner meets Visa through five programmes on Visa Partner, one developer platform, one acquiring platform with its own developer centre, and a client website renamed Visa Access (Visa Partner Programs · Visa Developer Center · Visa, Developer Center · Visa, Log).

OwnerVisa Inc., a Delaware corporation, with Visa Europe Limited as the separately supervised European scheme entity.(10-K)
ClientsNearly 14,500 financial institutions issuing or acquiring on Visa products.(FY2025 10-K)
Volume, fiscal 202517 trillion dollars of payments and cash volume, 329 billion transactions, nearly 5 billion credentials.(FY2025 10-K)

How a partner gets in

A bank applies for a licence through Visa Access after a regional team confirms eligibility, and the review runs on four axes: regulatory permissions, financial and compliance standing, and the rest (Visa's Licensing Program). Everyone who is not a bank is an agent. A member must register every third-party agent through Program Request Management, per acquirer, after a senior officer's review and an on-site inspection (Visa Core Rules). The published agent fee schedule dates from 2016, 5,000 dollars initial and annual for ISOs and payment facilitators, and the only published processing time is from the same FAQ, five to seven business days (Visa, Third Party Agent Registration Program Frequently Asked). Visa Partner now offers a self-service registration tool with three paths, ending in a business ID and a public directory listing (Visa Partner). Fintechs take Fast Track, which is eligibility criteria and enablement partners, with cost benefits described and no prices (Visa Partner · Visa, Fintech Fast Track). Technology vendors take Visa Ready, and one track publishes both a timeline and a cost (Visa Ready Program · Visa, Tap to Phone). ATM deployers are ISO-ATM agents, and an ATM must be owned or sponsored by a Visa or Plus client to qualify (Visa, Third Party Agent Registration Program).

What is sold, and what is mandatory

Value-added services were 10.9 billion dollars in fiscal 2025, sold in four portfolios through about 450 specialised sales staff (Visa 10-K 2025 · Visa 2025 Investor Day). On the issuing side the catalogue runs from processing (Visa DPS, Pismo) through tokens, risk scoring, disputes and stand-in authorisation to a Flex Credential (Visa 10-K 2025 · Visa Core Rules). Some of it is not optional. Account Updater enrolment is mandatory for issuers in most regions, alias directory participation is mandatory in three regions, and in Europe Visa auto-enrols every issuer in its authorisation risk score (Visa Core Rules). On the acquiring side the offer is the Visa Acceptance Platform under the Cybersource and Authorize.net brands, a merchant screening service that acquirers in three regions must use, and Tap to Phone with more than 20 million transacting devices (Visa 10-K 2025 · Visa Core Rules). Disputes run through Visa Resolve Online, which merchants never log into (Visa Resolve Online · Chargeback, What Is Visa Resolve Online (VROL)?). Money movement is Visa Direct, more than 12.5 billion transactions for more than 650 partners, and no fintech can take it to production without a licensed acquirer as sponsor (Visa 10-K 2025 · Getting Started with Visa Direct).

Fees, seen from outside

Merchants do not pay interchange directly. They pay a negotiated discount to their acquirer (Visa, Regulations & Fees). Canada is the one market where Visa publishes its acquiring network assessment, 0.09 percent on all Canadian-acquired volume (Visa Canada Standard Acquiring Network Assessment Fees). The Department of Justice complaint describes the debit side the schedules do not: per-transaction network fees, a fixed monthly acquirer fee since 2012, and routing contracts with volume cliffs (Complaint, United States v. Visa). The UK regulator found core scheme and processing fees to acquirers rose at least 25 percent since 2017 and has now imposed transparency and pricing-governance directions on Visa and Mastercard (Payment Systems Regulator, MR22/1.10 Market review of card scheme · Payment Systems Regulator, PS26/1 Market review of card scheme). Since November 2025 a superseding injunctive settlement with U.S. merchants has been before the court (Visa 10-Q 2026).

Rules and mandates in the window

Non-compliance follows a published ladder from a 1,000 dollar case fee upward, with Visa keeping full discretion to waive or deviate (Visa Core Rules). The Acquirer Monitoring Program replaced three programmes in April 2025 with one count-based ratio, and enforcement began October 1, 2025 (Visa Acquirer Monitoring Program Overview · Digital Transactions, Navigating the Visa Acquirer Monitoring Program). April 2026 brought rules for agentic transactions through digital wallets, a global scope for the member API-usage rule, and retirement of the separate Visa Direct processing guides (Visa Core Rules). From October 24, 2026 members must disclose every numeric identifier of each third-party agent (Visa Core Rules). Since April 18, 2026 any member using an API through the Developer Center is bound to its terms unless a bespoke agreement says otherwise (Visa Core Rules).

Support, as published

The developer platform publishes an email address, a contact form and an AI chatbot whose answers the terms say are not a communication with Visa (Visa Developer Center, Frequently Asked Questions · Visa Developer Center, Terms of Use · Visa Developer Center). No phone, hours or response commitment is published (Visa Developer Center, Frequently Asked Questions). Where no bespoke agreement applies, the terms say Visa has no obligation to support it (Visa Developer Center, Terms of Use · Visa Core Rules). A non-member gets support from its sponsoring member (Visa Developer Center, Terms of Use). Visa ran a peer-support developer community of 26,100 members, and its site did not answer on the day of reading (Visa Developer Community, Home). The acquiring side is different: a one-to-two business day response to developer requests, a public status page, chat and cases behind sign-in, and more than twenty country phone numbers (Visa Acceptance Solutions, Contact us · Visa Acceptance Solutions Status · Visa Acceptance Solutions, Home · Visa Acceptance Solutions, Support). Clients are assumed to have a named account executive, and the account model pairs a Client Success manager with a separate sales owner (Visa Ready Program · Visa Inc. careers, Director Client Success). Visa University sells paid training with exam-based certifications (Visa University, Payments Fundamentals · Visa Certification).

Twenty-four months

The Department of Justice sued in September 2024 over debit (Complaint, United States v. Visa). Featurespace was acquired in December 2024 and Pismo in January 2024, and Mexico's new antitrust commission rejected the Prosa majority stake in February 2026 (Visa 10-K 2025 · Electronic Payments International, Mexico antitrust regulator blocks Visa bid). The onboarding dashboard was redesigned in September 2025 and sign-in moved to a universal login with mandatory MFA in November 2025 (Visa Developer Center · Visa Developer Center, Frequently Asked Questions). Visa published a documentation MCP server on a sandbox host in November 2025 (GitHub, Documentation MCP Server · GitHub, gemini-extension.json at commit 65af8cb, visa/ai). In April 2026 it added an npm command-line package described as AI-powered payments for Claude Code (npm registry, @visa/cli). The rulebook's April 2026 edition opened the door to agentic transactions (Visa Core Rules). Visa's SEC filings no longer mention the developer platform at all (SEC, EDGAR Full-Text Search results).

The portal, walked

Visa Developer Center is among the most open of the six front doors read in this study. A stranger can read every product's overview and most products' documentation, filter the catalogue by the six audiences Visa names and by fifteen capabilities, read error codes, certificates guidance and monthly release notes, and reach a registration form in one click. Twenty of seventy-three products are restricted, and some, such as Visa Token Service, limit their documentation to approved users (Visa Developer Center, Browse Products · Visa Token Service). The account buys a project, sandbox credentials, the Playground, sample code, SDKs and implementation guides (Visa Developer Quick Start · Visa Developer Center Playground). A contract buys certification and production. The page itself says so: all products are free to use in Sandbox but require the reader to contact Visa for pricing and commercial terms (observed September 25, 2026).

Mastercard

Mastercard Incorporated · Purchase, New York · more than 220 countries and territories in the filing, more than 210 on its own site · issuers, acquirers and processors, merchants, service providers, network enablement partners, fintechs, developers

Mastercard runs a franchise and a developer platform, and connects them by company ID. Every participant is approved as a Customer, licensed and assigned an ICA number and a Business Relationship Type, and that type is what decides which of the ninety-one developer products a company may take to production (Mastercard Rules · Mastercard Rules, Definitions · Mastercard, Business Relationship Type (BRT)). The developer side is the most open in this study: every documentation page has a markdown twin, the specifications download logged out, sandbox credentials are self-service for most APIs, and a public status page reports each API's health (Mastercard Developers, Working with llms.txt · Mastercard Developers, Mastercom Dispute Processing API · Mastercard Developers, Quick Start Guide · Mastercard Developers, API Status). The franchise side is the most gated: rule changes are announced inside Mastercard Connect, and the client portal is a hard login wall (Mastercard, Chargebacks Made Simple Guide · Mastercard Connect).

OwnerMastercard Incorporated, with Mastercard International Incorporated as the licensing entity. No ownership change since 2020.(10-K)
Cards in force3.7 billion Mastercard and Maestro cards at December 31, 2025, unchanged at June 30, 2026.(10-K, 10-Q · Mastercard Incorporated Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial)
Volume, 202510.6 trillion dollars gross dollar volume, 175.5 billion switched transactions.(FY2025 10-K)
Acceptance"Hundreds of millions" of locations in the FY2025 filing. The year before it said about 150 million locations and over 250 million digital access points.(10-K series · Mastercard 10-K 2024)
Message modelBoth. A Dual Message System and a Single Message System, with Maestro as the PIN debit brand and Cirrus the ATM brand.(Mastercom docs, Federal Reserve, 10-K · Federal Reserve, Regulation II · Mastercard 10-K 2025)
Participation typesPrincipal, Affiliate, Affiliate Sponsoring Customer, Payment Transfer Activity Customer, Digital Activity Customer. Mastercard alone decides the level.(Mastercard Rules)
RulebooksPublic PDFs: Mastercard Rules, 503 pages dated June 2, 2026, Transaction Processing Rules and Security Rules. The 1,582-page Chargeback Guide of May 2026 was no longer linked from the rules page by September 10.(Mastercard rules page · Mastercard Rules · Mastercard, Chargeback Guide Merchant Edition)
Rule changesAnnouncements in the Technical Resource Center on Mastercard Connect, behind its sign-in. The Mastercard Rules open with a summary of changes that cites them by number.(Mastercard Rules · Mastercard Connect, walked · Mastercard Rules)
InterchangeA public U.S. schedule effective April 17, 2026. Consumer credit at the Merit III Base rate from 1.65 percent plus 10 cents. Regulated debit 0.05 percent plus 21 cents.(U.S. interchange PDF)
Rebates and incentives, 202520,522 million dollars paid to customers, up 16 percent.(FY2025 10-K)
Developer platform91 products logged out, 58 tagged for issuers, 42 for merchants, 38 for acquirers, 11 for fintechs. No API pricing published.(Mastercard Developers · Mastercard Developers llms.txt)
Published turnaroundsMastercom: licence agreement loaded in five to seven business days. Mastercard Send: registration two to four weeks.(Mastercom and Send docs · Mastercard Send Disbursements Onboarding Checklist)

How a partner gets in

A Principal or Affiliate must be a regulated financial institution, meet financial requirements Mastercard sets and may assess subjectively, and hold AML and sanctions programmes as a condition of the licence (Mastercard Rules). The application is a public Qualtrics form titled Universal Onboarding Template (Mastercard Send Registration and Eligibility). Since May 20, 2025 a Principal needs Mastercard's approval before sponsoring a program manager, and Mastercard stopped designating new Type I processors on the same day (Mastercard Rules). Third parties do not register themselves. The sponsoring customer registers each service provider in My Company Manager on Mastercard Connect, pays an initial and an annual fee whose amounts are not public, and carries the liability (Mastercard Rules). Operationally significant providers can contract directly as Network Enablement Partners, in tiers from Core to Platinum with a light package for small payment facilitators, and some roles must (Mastercard Rules · Mastercard, Network enablement partners). Fintechs are sold Product Express, where card issuance runs through a BIN sponsor and pre-certified processors (Mastercard Product Express), and Engage, a free marketplace of qualified enablers with a public directory (Mastercard Engage · Mastercard Engage Partner Program).

What is sold, and what is mandatory

Value-added services were about 11 billion dollars in 2024 with a high-teens growth target, sold to fintechs, payment facilitators, acquirers, issuers, governments, small businesses and large merchants, and distributed through platforms, integrators, processors and other networks (Mastercard Investment Community Meeting presentation, November 13). For issuers the catalogue is tokens (MDES and its Token Connect and customer-service APIs), processing, stand-in, network fraud scoring, Click to Pay enablement and loyalty (Mastercard Developers llms.txt index · Mastercard Processing Core APIs · Mastercard 10-K 2025 · Mastercard, Issuer Enablement in Click). For acquirers, MATCH Pro is mandatory before signing a merchant, its legacy files were decommissioned on January 1, 2026, and Onboard Risk Check is offered as API and as a screen inside Connect (Mastercard, MATCH Pro · Mastercard, Onboard Risk Check). Disputes run through Mastercom, the mandatory channel, with a pre-chargeback collaboration step, a next-generation Extended API still migrating, and a first-party-trust liability shift for merchants with evidence (Mastercard, Transaction Processing Rules · Mastercard Developers, Dispute Resolution Cycle (Mastercom) · Mastercard Developers llms.txt · Mastercard Developers llms.txt index). Money movement is Mastercard Send and Move, available only to or through a licensed acquirer or issuer (Mastercard Developers llms.txt index · Mastercard Send Disbursements Onboarding Checklist). On the acceptance side, Mastercard Gateway and the 2025 Merchant Cloud bundle sit outside the switch, and Agent Pay launched in 2025 on top of tokens and disputes (Mastercard Developers llms.txt index · Mastercard 10-K 2025).

Fees, seen from outside

Mastercard sets default interchange and disclaims any role in acquirer-to-merchant pricing (Mastercard Interchange Fees and Rates Explained). The four network fee streams are named in the filing, and 2025 gross assessments ran to 11.0 billion domestic, 12.0 billion cross-border and 15.9 billion transaction processing (Mastercard 10-K 2025). The U.S. ATM interchange is public and tiered by the issuer's quarterly ATM volume (Mastercard 2026-2027 U.S. Region Interchange Programs). Developer terms describe paid API subscriptions billed monthly, quarterly or yearly, but no rate is published (Mastercard Developers Terms of Use · Mastercard Developers llms.txt). The UK regulator's findings on scheme fees apply to Mastercard as to Visa, and a November 2025 revised U.S. merchant settlement replaced one the court had denied (Payment Systems Regulator, MR22/1.10 Market review of card scheme · Mastercard 10-K 2025).

Rules and mandates in the window

Noncompliance runs in three categories, with Category A assessments from 25,000 dollars to 100,000 per violation within twelve months, an appeal to the Chief Franchise Officer within thirty days, and variances requested only through a tool on Connect (Mastercard Rules). Account data compromises must be notified within 24 hours (Mastercard, Security Rules and Procedures Merchant Edition). Mandates in the window include the end of undefined authorisations in June 2025, transaction link identifiers in October 2025, a stablecoin transaction type in April 2026, near-real-time age verification in June 2026, a card-level spend score in October 2026, and monitoring that moves from merchant to sub-merchant identifiers in April 2027 (Merchant Advisory Group, Brand Release Updates · SoFi Tech Solutions, Card Network Mandates · Marqeta, Card Network Certifications 2026 · SLYCE360, Mastercard GMAP Explained). Practitioners say the bulletins themselves go only to member institutions through Connect (SLYCE360, Mastercard GMAP Explained). The public Mastercom documentation summarises its own API changes and usually names the bulletin that holds the effective dates (Mastercard Developers, Mastercom Announcements).

Support, as published

Urgent partner inquiries go to Customer Technical Services by phone and the rest to a Support Case Management application on Connect (Mastercard Rules · Mastercard, Release Notes and Dates). On the developer side a ticket needs sign-in, the forum is public with four categories, and implementation help is routed to Engage partners (Support at Mastercard Developers · Mastercard, Home · Mastercard Developers (home)). The forum also records friction: sandbox access under review, a 403 from a pending sandbox, a developer asking how to load sample claims (Mastercard Developers Forum, Sandbox API blocked by Incapsula WAF · Mastercard Developers Forum, Mastercom Sandbox · Mastercard Developers Forum, Receiving 403 while consuming). Training is Mastercard Academy, by region, whose landing shows selectors and no public catalogue (Mastercard Academy). A Dispute Resolution Management team trains issuers, acquirers and processors on chargebacks (Mastercard, Chargebacks Made Simple Guide).

Twenty-four months

Domestic switching in China began in 2024 through the NetsUnion joint venture (Mastercard 10-K 2024). Maestro's European run-off continued, with issuers replacing expired cards with Debit Mastercard since July 2023 (Mastercard, Blog from Valerie Nowak). Merchant Cloud launched in 2025, Agent Pay in 2025, and Recorded Future became a Mastercard threat-intelligence service (Mastercard 10-K 2025). On the developer platform, FAPI 2.0 OAuth arrived in May 2026, automatic production mTLS certificates in June 2026 and a project history audit trail in July 2026, alongside a public MCP server and an agent toolkit (Mastercard, Blog · Mastercard Developers Agent Toolkit). About 130 crypto co-brand programmes ran on the network in 2025 (Mastercard 10-K 2025). The FY2025 filing names Discover as a competitor now owned by Capital One (Mastercard 10-K 2025).

The portal, walked

Mastercard Developers reads like the developer site of a software company. The catalogue of ninety-one products is public and filterable by six audiences, almost every product's documentation opens logged out with the same sidebar shape (Mastercard Developers), a public status page reports each API's health for sandbox and production, and llms.txt files sit in the footer of every page. The account is self-service in three stated steps and buys a project and, for most APIs, sandbox keys (Mastercard Developers, Quick Start Guide). Production credentials need company verification and turn on only when Mastercard approves the production request (Mastercard Developers, Quick Start Guide · Mastercard, Company Verification). Production certificates have been issued automatically since June 2026 (Mastercard, Blog). Support by ticket needs the account. Everything else, including a forum and a directory of implementation partners, does not (observed September 25, 2026).

Seen in demonstrations

Mastercard's own channels carry the most complete public record of any network. An official tutorial shows a developer signing up with an email and a password, filling a four-field project form and landing on a dashboard with sandbox credentials, with production left for another day. Two videos add what the desk research missed. The Mastercard Gateway's test merchant comes from the merchant's bank or payment service provider, and Click to Pay is switched on by that provider. Training modules show payment facilitators registered by their acquirer through Mastercard Connect, and issuers reporting questionable merchants to a mailbox.

American Express

American Express Company · New York · network partners in about 110 countries and territories · issuers, acquirers and processors, merchants, service providers, fintechs, developers

Amex sells a licence, then hands the rules over. A partner on the American Express network is a third party licensed as an issuer or an acquirer, and nothing that binds it is public before the licence: the network rulebook, the fee schedule and the specifications all arrive after signature (American Express Global Network Policy). What a stranger can read is the merchant side, a developer portal of sixteen products, and a service-provider certification programme that charges nothing to join (American Express, Merchant Regulations · American Express Developers product catalogue · AMEX Enabled Frequently Asked Questions).

OwnerAmerican Express Company, a bank holding company supervised by the Federal Reserve. Largest holder Berkshire Hathaway at 22.1 percent.(10-K and proxy · American Express proxy 2026)
Cards in force, 2025152.8 million, of which 66.2 million issued by network partners.(FY2025 10-K)
Volume on partner cards, 2025227.2 billion dollars processed, about twelve percent of network volume of 1,897 billion.(FY2025 10-K)
Partner footprintAbout 110 countries and territories in the FY2025 filing, 120 the year before, 103 in 2021.(10-K series · American Express 10-K 2024 · American Express 10-K 2021)
Merchant locationsOver 170 million at year-end 2025, a count that includes payfac and wallet reach and 37 million in China. The earnings boilerplate says over a hundred million.(Annual Report, 8-K · American Express 10-K 2025 · American Express Reports Full-Year)
Message modelSeparate authorisation and financial-submission specifications. Debit added in 2021.(Amex specifications · American Express 10-K 2021)
Regulation IIAbsent from the Federal Reserve's network tables, which exclude three-party systems.(Federal Reserve · Federal Reserve, Regulation II)
OptBlue ceiling3 million dollars of estimated annual Amex volume from April 17, 2026, up from 1 million. Eight industries carry no ceiling.(OptBlue programme updates)
RulebooksMerchant Regulations and the Merchant Operating Guide are public PDFs, April and October. The network-side BOP manual is confidential.(Amex rules pages · American Express, Merchant Operating Guide · American Express network, Business and Operational Policies)
Partner bulletinNetwork Participant Updates, the second Friday of each month, with Special Bulletins as needed.(GNS network policy)
Public API productsEighteen in the catalogue endpoint, five of them with the specification invite-only.(Amex Developers · American Express, Account and Transaction API Overview)
Certified service providersOver 1,200 claimed under AMEX Enabled, across 17 product portfolios.(GNS site, Vendor)

Three programmes, three doors

Global Network Services licenses banks to issue Amex-branded cards or to acquire local merchants, and monetises the licence as royalties, fees and per-transaction amounts (American Express 10-K 2025). The issuer rate each partner is paid is negotiated and never published (American Express 10-K 2025). Certification is a mandatory network service for both sides: issuers complete host and payment-product certification, acquirers complete host and terminal certification (American Express Certification), with an eight-step representative-led host process, a self-accreditation route for qualifying acquirers and a free host simulator (U.S. Payments Forum, EMV Testing and Certification White Paper). Fintechs do not licence directly. They arrive through issuer-processors admitted to the Agile Partnership Platform, Marqeta in February 2025 and Lithic in May 2025, with a sponsor bank issuing (Lithic Expands Platform to Offer More Payment · Payments Dive, Fintech Cardless taps Amex network). The public fintech page carries positioning and no application (American Express network, Partners).

OptBlue is the acquiring door. Acquirers, processors and payment facilitators contract directly with small merchants and set the price. Amex charges the merchant no wholesale fee and the participant is the merchant's single servicing contact (American Express Card Acceptance Pricing · American Express, Credit Card Processing for Small Businesses). Thirty-two participants are named on the public page (American Express, OptBlue: Credit Card Processing). What is not public is how an acquirer becomes one. Amex publishes no process for joining OptBlue, and the participant rulebook is named but not published (American Express, Credit Card Processing for Small Businesses · American Express, OptBlue Program Merchant Eligibility). Payment facilitators under 250 million dollars of annual Amex volume ride under a certified participant (Payments Facilitator Acceptance of American Express Cards). Canada is the one market where the wholesale schedule is public, tiered by industry and ticket size with a 0.12 percent participation fee and a 0.30 percent card-not-present fee (American Express, Network Assessment Fees).

AMEX Enabled is the door for everyone who builds: terminal, card, mobile, 3-D Secure and tokenisation providers, laboratories and platforms register in three steps, pay nothing, and work inside a dashboard with a certification journey, a document library and DocuSign contracts (American Express network, Partners · AMEX Enabled Frequently Asked Questions · AMEX Enabled Service Provider Program). Registration is not approval, since a product must still pass certification before anyone may use it (AMEX Enabled Service Provider Program). The programme's own entry hostname did not answer on the day of reading and the working entry is the service-provider page (AMEX Enabled Service Provider Program). POS software vendors join the Integrated Payments Providers track with a named team for test cards and certification questions (American Express, Partners).

What a licensed partner sees

Once licensed, the partner lives in the Knowledge Base, the gateway to every network service: FraudNet, OpsNet, File Tracker, the Token Requester tool, service enrolment and a participant directory (American Express, Knowledge Base · American Express Global Network). Access requests are handled by GNS User Services with a stated three-business-day turnaround (American Express, Knowledge Base). Policy arrives as manuals twice a year, interim changes as the monthly bulletin, and specification mandates six months ahead (American Express Global Network Policy · American Express network, Business and Operational Policies · American Express, Notification of Specification Changes (NOSC)). Urgent operational notices are posted inside the Knowledge Base, not on a status page (American Express, Insights). Training is a named function, Network Partner Learning Solutions, with an essentials curriculum, six compliance modules covering more than fifty policies, and webinars in two formats (American Express, Partner Learning · American Express, Partners). The public webinar list has not been updated since 2022 and the public news hub carried no dated articles when read (American Express, Partner Learning · American Express, News).

Twenty-four months

The window opened with two merchant class actions attacking the anti-steering rules under OptBlue (American Express Annual Report 2025) and a 230 million dollar resolution of the small-business sales-practices investigations in January 2025 (American Express 8-K). Leadership swapped in February 2025, with Anna Marrs taking Global Merchant and Network Services (American Express, Exhibit 99.1). The network opened to fintechs through Marqeta and Lithic, and Coinbase launched a card on it (Lithic Expands Platform to Offer More Payment · American Express, New Coinbase One Card). The OptBlue ceiling tripled in April 2026 (American Express, OptBlue Sales Agent). The same month Amex unveiled the Agentic Commerce Experiences developer kit with a purchase-protection promise for registered agents, and later agreed to buy Hypercard, a fintech that had launched on the network through the Agile Partnership Platform (American Express Debuts Agentic Commerce Experiences (ACE) · American Express to Acquire Hyper, Adding). In May 2026 Amazon moved its business co-brand to U.S. Bank on Mastercard (Amazon's New Prime Business). In August 2026 Amex signed three Thai banks as acquiring partners (American Express Expands Card Acceptance). The reintroduced Credit Card Competition Act exempts cards where issuer and network are commonly owned, which is Amex's position (Senator Durbin, Durbin, Marshall Reintroduce The Credit Card Competition · Kilpatrick, Credit Card Competition Act).

The portal, walked

American Express Developers is small and readable. Sixteen products sit in one menu, each opening on an overview (American Express Developers, walked). A stranger can read each unlocked API reference to the endpoint, the sample code and the version history (American Express Developers, walked). Some references are locked for security reasons, and some products are not listed at all (American Express, High-Level Process · American Express, Account and Transaction API Overview). The path is written on the landing in four steps that end with "get access" after sign-up (American Express Developers, walked). The portal reads as one product's documentation site for a closed network: the catalogue is a menu, the search is a product filter, and the support route is a ticket form with its hours stated (observed September 25, 2026).

Discover Global Network

Discover Global Network · Discover Network, PULSE and Diners Club International · owned by Capital One since May 18, 2025 · issuers, acquirers and processors, merchants, ATM acquirers, network alliances, fintechs, developers

Discover sells a relationship and meets its partners through ten doors. The partnering page offers no application steps, fees or timelines and positions the network as consultative, with the contact form as the way in (Discover Global Network, How We Partner). Behind the form the family runs ten partner login pages, each built for particular partner types (Discover Network Service Center · Discover Global Network, Get Started · PULSE Network, Client Support). The Developer Center is invite-only while the acquirer portal is self-registered (Discover, FAQ · Discover EASI Portal Login). The network is now Capital One's, its 2025 debit reissue has more than doubled network volume, and the filing groups the three brands as the Global Payment Network (Capital One Financial, Exhibit 99.1 · Capital One 10-Q 2026 · Capital One 10-K 2025).

OwnerCapital One Financial Corporation, from May 18, 2025. The Federal Reserve approved the merger on April 18, 2025 and fined Discover 100 million dollars the same day.(Capital One, Federal Reserve · Federal Reserve Board announces approval)
Brand familyDiscover Network, PULSE and Diners Club International, marketed together as Discover Global Network.(FY2024 10-K)
Volume, FY2024621.9 billion dollars across the networks: PULSE 328.3 billion, Diners Club 41.4 billion, Network Partners 32.8 billion, the rest proprietary.(Discover FY2024 10-K)
Volume after the merger189.6 billion dollars in the second quarter of 2026 against 74.0 billion a year earlier, after Capital One reissued its debit cards onto the network.(Capital One 10-Q, 10-K · Capital One 10-K 2025)
Cards and reachMore than 439 million cards and 185 countries and territories on the landing page. 378 million cards on the Our Unique Network page, citing 2024 data.(discoverglobalnetwork.com, Vendor · Discover Global Network, Our Unique Payments Network)
AlliancesMore than 30 network alliances by signed agreement, carried on the same IIN ranges an acquirer enables for Discover. The merchant page names eight alliance card brands to accept, with JCB and UnionPay processed only in certain territories, including the U.S.(discoverglobalnetwork.com · Discover Global Network, Tools to Enable Payments · Discover Global Network, Accept Global Cardholders)
Diners ClubA licensee network: more than 40 issuers in more than 35 countries, none of them Discover itself.(10-K, DGN site · Discover Global Network, Our Unique Payments Network)
Regulation IIPULSE averaged 27 cents per transaction in 2024. Discover debit is entirely exempt at 83 cents. The Fed's order confirms Regulation II does not reach three-party systems.(Federal Reserve · Federal Reserve order 2025-10)
RulebookOperating regulations and program documents, updated semi-annually, not public. The U.S. acquirer fee chart is confidential and sits behind an acquirer-issued code.(DGN service center · Discover Global Network, U.S. Acquirer Interchange Pricing)
Public feesCanada only: acquirer assessment 0.063 percent, international processing fee 0.40 percent, international card sales from 1.20 percent, effective April 17, 2026.(DGN Canada schedule)
Public API productsSeven on the Developer Center's Explore page, twelve with OpenAPI specifications on the Partner Product Portal. The full list is visible only after login.(Discover Developer Center, Partner Product Portal · Discover Partner Product Portal · Discover Partner Product Portal · developer.discover.com, FAQs)
Support hoursOperations Center for processors in Eastern business hours with twelve holidays. A 24x7 Command Center for connectivity incidents.(DGN service center)

How a partner gets in

The contact form is the front door and it asks who you are before anything else, from nine U.S. partner types (Discover Global Network, Contact Us). Acquirers and processors register for EASI, which is open to eighteen named company types through a multi-stage application that collects contact, company, signing-authority and business-purpose details before credentials are emailed (Discover Global Network, EASI Portal Registration). Developers cannot register. New users submit the contact form and wait for a representative, and collaborators are added by invitation (developer.discover.com, FAQs). After approval a partner gets an organisation and an application with credentials, an API Plan that mirrors the signed service agreement and sets the rate limits no page publishes, and a second factor in the form of a consumer application certificate that can be downloaded once (partner.discoverglobalnetwork.com, Going Live with Discover · Discover Partner Product Portal). PULSE participants sponsor merchants, processors and ISOs and carry liability for them, under agreements that auto-renew without fixed terms (Discover 10-K 2024). Diners Club issuing is handled by outreach to a brand mailbox, with no published steps (Discover Global Network, Diners Club Issuing). Fintechs are assembled through BIN sponsors, processors and program managers and are not contracted directly (Discover Global Network, Fintech Partnerships). Device and product vendors pass Discover type approval and appear in a public Partner Directory last updated May 21, 2026 (Discover Global Network, Partner Directory).

What is sold

The public catalogue is organised by theme, with no partner-type view: enable payments, fraud and security, PCI compliance, issuing and co-creation, technology platforms, debit and ATM (Discover Network). The technology layer is D-PAS and D-PAS Connect for EMV, Discover Digital Exchange for wallets and tokens with developer APIs, and Discover Commerce Xchange (Discover Network · Discover Digital Exchange DDX). Stored Token Services holds merchant-bound and wallet-bound tokens and is enabled through a certified partner or directly (Discover Global Network, Stored Token Services). Fraud products are Enhanced Decisioning, ProtectBuy and a High Brand Risk programme that adds registration duties for acquirers in named verticals (Discover Network · Discover Global Network, High Brand Risk (HBR) Program). PULSE sells issuers five things, including gateway access to STAR, NYCE, Interlink, Maestro, Plus and Cirrus from one connection, a full-service debit processing offer covering Discover, Mastercard and Visa programmes, and Discover Debit for regional banks and credit unions (PULSE, Issuers · PULSE, Debit Processing and Gateways). ATM acquirers get the domestic network and exclusive access to Discover and Diners Club cards (PULSE, ATM Acquirers). The security programme is DISC, with a PCI relief scheme for merchants above 75 percent EMV, and Discover is a founding member of the PCI council (Discover Information Security and Compliance · Discover Global Network, Validation and Reporting Requirements · Discover 10-K 2024).

Fees, seen from outside

Discover says it competes for partners on incentives, rebates, issuer fees and switch fees, and publishes none of the amounts (Discover 10-K 2024). Alliance partners pay network assessment, discount and interchange fees (Discover 10-K 2024). PULSE switch fees are per-transaction amounts in participation agreements, with fixed-term pricing for some (Discover 10-K 2024). The Federal Reserve found Discover misclassified consumer cards as commercial from 2007 to at least 2023, overcharging merchants, and the counterparty restitution liability stood at 1.2 billion dollars (Federal Reserve order 2025-10 · Discover 10-K 2024). A merchant class settlement over the misclassification received final approval on May 20, 2026 (Capital One 10-Q 2026). Discover reports, as a risk, that Visa's arrangements with merchants and acquirers discourage routing debit to PULSE (Discover 10-K 2024).

Support, as published

Support is segmented by role and mostly by mailbox: partnership, fraud solutions, interchange, and a single address for partners outside the United States and Canada (Discover Global Network, Contact Us). Processors have a named Account Executive as their escalation point, and issuers separate toll-free numbers for credit, debit and prepaid (Discover Global Network, Contact Us). Day-to-day operations for acquirers run through EASI's Message Center (Discover Global Network, Get Started). Data compromises are reported by phone within 48 hours (Discover Global Network, Contact Us). There is no partner academy. The PCI training page points to the PCI council's programmes (Discover Global Network, PCI Compliance Education and Training). PULSE publishes hours for its sales line and a two-business-day callback on web requests, and names help desks by persona (PULSE, Client Support). Discover positions the relationship as co-creation with network experts, and no ticketed desk is offered (Discover Global Network, How We Partner).

Twenty-four months

The Federal Reserve and the OCC approved the merger on April 18, 2025, with a consent order and a 100 million dollar fine over interchange overcharges, and the FDIC's parallel settlement carried a 150 million dollar penalty (Federal Reserve Board announces approval · Federal Reserve order 2025-10). The deal closed on May 18, 2025 and three Discover directors joined Capital One's board (Capital One Completes Acquisition). Jason Hanson leads the Global Payment Network on Capital One's executive committee, with senior transfers from Capital One into acceptance and network roles (Discover Global Payment Network Leadership Team). By February 2026 Capital One had substantially completed reissuing its legacy debit cards onto the network (Capital One 10-K 2025). In April 2026 trade press reported more than a hundred Discover application engineering jobs eliminated in the integration (Payments Dive, Which Discover jobs are disappearing). The Advanced Payments Portal login now carries a Capital One acquisition notice, and the SCIP form is still issued under DFS Services LLC (Discover Global Network, Advanced Payments Portal Login · Discover Global Network, Merchant Security Compliance Innovation Program (SCIP) Application).

The portals, walked

The Discover family meets its partners through ten front doors, most with their own registration (Discover Network Service Center · Discover Partner Product Portal · DFS Services, Discover Partner Product Portal). The marketing site carries the catalogue and the contact form. The Developer Center is a gateway with a welcome line, a button that leaves for the Partner Product Portal, and an FAQ that says access comes by invitation. The Partner Product Portal lists twelve products with public specifications and a resources page that names the rest: the Release Compliance Tool for testing and certification, the Disputes Portal, EASI for acquirers and processors, Web Merchant Boarding. The site's own Log In lands on the Fraud and Risk Center, which lists four more client portals in a side panel. A stranger counts ten places to sign in before finding the one that is theirs (observed September 25, 2026 · Discover Developer Center, walked · Discover Partner Product Portal, walked · Discover EASI Portal Login, walked).

Diners Club International

Diners Club International · a licensee network inside Discover Global Network · owned by Capital One since May 18, 2025 · franchise issuers in 35 to 44 countries, acquirers through Discover, corporate clients through local issuers

Diners Club is a franchise, and the network owner issues nothing. Outside the United States the licensees issue the cards and set their terms, so the partner-facing product is a licence per market, exclusive in most and non-exclusive in some (Capital One 10-K 2025 · Discover Global Network, Diners Club International Issuing). Everything a licensee then needs sits inside Discover's portals: EASI for acquirers and processors, a ServiceNow site for current issuers, the Developer Center by invitation (Discover Global Network, Tools to Enable Payments · Discover Global Network, Get Started · Discover Developer Center). The public record on Diners is thin. Most of what can be read is the brand's own claims, which this profile labels as such.

OwnerCapital One, through the Discover acquisition completed May 18, 2025.(Capital One)
ModelA network of licensees, generally financial institutions, that issue cards and or provide acceptance. The owner keeps a strong licensee base as a named risk.(Capital One 10-K)
Issuers44 on dinersclub.com, counted as franchises with active participation agreements. "35+ countries" on the Discover site.(dinersclub.com, DGN, Vendor · Discover Global Network, About Diners Club International)
AcceptanceMore than 185 countries and territories together with Discover Network. More than 1.2 million ATMs in over 130 countries.(DGN, Vendor · Discover Global Network, Diners Club International Issuing)
Volume41.4 billion dollars in FY2024 in Discover's last filing. The brand's site cites the whole network's 634 billion.(Discover 10-K, dinersclub.com · About Diners Club)
InterchangeNegotiated per issuing organisation and volume-based. No Diners schedule on the public interchange page, which offers United States and Canada only.(DGN · Discover Global Network, Acquirer Interchange Pricing)
Rules and specsBehind the Discover Service Center login. No public rulebook.(DGN service center)
Regulation IIOutside the rule today as a three-party network, a status Capital One flags as changeable.(Capital One 10-K)

What is sold, to whom

To issuers, Diners offers premium, co-branded, prepaid and debit consumer products, commercial programmes with expense management, and the loyalty layer the brand is known for: lounges, Destinations content and privileges (Discover Global Network, Diners Club International Issuing). The commercial set of SMB, corporate and multinational cards with virtual card numbers and corporate travel accounts is delivered through local issuers, and the Tracker reporting tool is sold as a PDF (Discover Global Network, Diners Club Commercial Products). Merchants accept Diners through their existing acquirer, and the brand's site offers a find-an-acquirer page and no application (Accept Discover Global Network · Diners Club International, Card Programs). Becoming an issuer is a contact form or a brand mailbox (Diners Club International, Business Payment Solutions · Discover Global Network, Diners Club Issuing). Device vendors go through Discover type approval into the public Partner Directory (Discover Global Network, Partner Directory).

Support, as published

Cardholder support goes to the local franchise, and the network's help centre is a country selector (Diners Club International, Help Center · Diners Club International). Business enquiries from the Diners site land on Discover Global Network's shared contact form (Diners Club International, Businesses). Current issuers work in a ServiceNow-hosted portal, acquirers and processors in EASI's Message Center (Discover Global Network, Get Started). A public news stream, Club Connections, carries the partner announcements with dates and needs no login (Diners Club International, Press Releases). An online dispute resolution site exists at odr.dinersclub.com without saying who it is for (Diners Club International, Online Dispute Resolution).

Twenty-four months

The network changed owner in May 2025 (Capital One Financial 8-K). Since then the franchise has grown at the edges: Nium and Pax2pay issuing virtual cards for travel, BRAC Bank's Emerald card in Bangladesh, Moorwand adding UK acquiring to its issuing licence in December 2025, Sparkasse Pay's co-badged Diners and Mastercard card in Slovenia, Uzcard's alliance for acceptance across Uzbekistan, and ISX Financial's flykk debit card in the EU and UK on September 24, 2026 (Nium Launches Diners Club International Card · Pax2pay Partners with Diners Club International · BRAC Bank collaborates with Diners Club International · resources.dinersclub.com, Moorwand Ltd Expands Its Collaboration · resources.dinersclub.com, Sparkasse Pay introduces a new credit card · resources.dinersclub.com, UZCARD and Discover Network Announce Strategic Alliance · The new flykk Diners Club International Debit). The brand calls itself the fastest-growing global network by alliance count (ISX Financial and Diners Club International Launch).

The site, walked

Diners Club International's own site speaks to cardmembers and to corporate clients. There is no issuer, franchisee, acquirer or developer door in its navigation. A bank that wants to issue is told to search for its country and to contact the Club, and a current issuer signs in through a ServiceNow login linked from the Discover Global Network site. Partner news lives on a separate stream, Club Connections, which is where the franchise model shows: new issuers in Bangladesh and the United Kingdom, an acquiring collaboration, fintech card launches (observed September 25, 2026).

PULSE

PULSE · Houston · the debit and ATM network inside Discover Global Network · owned by Capital One since May 18, 2025 · issuers, ATM acquirers, merchants and acquirers, processors

PULSE publishes a client relationship and keeps every number inside it. The public site is organised by what it offers and by who the reader is, promises credentials within five business days, names its help desks by persona, and states no interchange, no switch fee, no participant count and no rule (PULSE Network, Log In / Register · PULSE Network, Client Support · PULSE Payments Network · PULSE ATM Network). The only rules-type document reachable logged out is the brand manual, and the public news feed has not been updated since August 2024 (PULSE Network, Client Support · PULSE Network, Insights & News). Most of what is readable is PULSE's own account of itself, labelled Vendor below.

OwnerCapital One, from May 18, 2025. The operating entity is PULSE Network LLC, a Delaware company.(Capital One, PULSE terms · PULSE Network, Terms of Use)
What it isAn EFT network giving debit issuers ATM access domestically and internationally plus U.S. merchant acceptance.(Capital One 10-K)
Volume328.3 billion dollars and 9.6 billion transactions in FY2024, the last year reported separately. Capital One no longer breaks PULSE out.(Discover 10-K, Capital One 10-K · Capital One 10-K 2025)
Regulation II29 cents per exempt transaction and 24 cents per covered transaction in the 2024 network data.(Federal Reserve)
ATMsMore than 400,000 in the United States, per PULSE.(pulsenetwork.com, Vendor)
Message modelSingle and dual message, with PIN debit on PULSE PAY and PINless on PULSE PAY Express.(pulsenetwork.com)
JoiningA sales call-back form, then an Account Executive. Participants sponsor merchants, processors and ISOs and carry their liability.(pulsenetwork.com, Discover 10-K · PULSE Network, Fraud Detection & Risk Mitigation · Discover 10-K 2024)
Gateway reachOne message format and one settlement point to thirteen named networks, including STAR, NYCE, Interlink, Maestro, Plus, Cirrus and Allpoint.(pulsenetwork.com · PULSE Network, Debit Processing & Gateways)
Fraud programmeDebitProtect on FICO Falcon, bundled for every participant, with Authorization Blocking as the premium tier.(pulsenetwork.com · PULSE Network, Fraud Detection & Risk Mitigation)
Gated toolsPULSE Debit Dashboard, ATM List Manager and PULSE Exchange behind the PULSE site login. The Marketing Hub signs in on a separate site.(pulsenetwork.com)

What is sold, to whom

Issuers are offered debit payments and transfers, processing and gateways, ATM access, fraud detection and the Discover Debit programme, a signature debit product for community banks and credit unions sold on an all-in fee with a one-page invoice and an ABA endorsement, at a fee level the site does not state (PULSE, Issuers · PULSE Network, Discover Debit). The processing offer is full-service signature debit for Discover, Mastercard and Visa programmes (PULSE Network, Debit Processing and Gateways). ATM acquirers get the domestic network, PULSE issuers and international partner networks, exclusive access to Discover and Diners Club cards, and a surcharge-free tie to MoneyPass (PULSE Network, ATM Acquirers). Merchants get PIN debit, PINless, e-commerce and mobile with routing choice (PULSE Network, Merchants). The Side-by-Side token service for card-on-file debit is enrolled by contact form and has no published specification or fee (PULSE Side-by-Side Token Service). PULSE markets API access and tokenisation to issuers and reaches no developer portal, reference, sandbox or SDK logged out (Why PULSE).

Support and advocacy

Support is segmented by partner type with named hotlines and mailboxes, and Partner Support Services bundles the Debit Dashboard, DebitProtect, the Marketing Hub, full disputes support and research and advocacy (PULSE Network, Client Support · PULSE Network, Partner Support Services). The sales line keeps weekday Central hours and web requests get a two-business-day callback (PULSE, Client Support). The dispute framework is not named publicly (PULSE Network, Merchants). The annual Debit Issuer Study is gated behind a form with its headline figures public: debit transactions up 4.6 percent, card-not-present at half of debit spend (2026 PULSE Debit Issuer Study). PULSE sits on EMVCo, the U.S. Payments Forum, the Faster Payments Council, the FIDO Alliance and the Merchant Advisory Group (About PULSE).

Twenty-four months

The network changed owner in May 2025 and Capital One's filing groups it into the Global Payment Network without a separate volume (Capital One 10-K 2025). The filing flags that PULSE merchants are largely not contractually committed and that competitor routing strategies can hurt its volume, a Regulation II risk (Capital One 10-K 2025). PULSE claims Regulation II compliance for card-not-present routing through PULSE PAY Express (PULSE Payments Network). The careers link now points to Capital One (About PULSE).

The site, walked

PULSE publishes the shape of a client relationship. There is no developer platform to publish. The site is organised by what it offers and by who the reader is, with a page each for issuers, ATM acquirers and merchants, and every one of those pages ends in the same support promise, "When you call, we answer." The client website sits behind a registration form, and the login page publishes a turnaround: credentials within five business days (PULSE Network, Log). Client Support lists a phone number, hours and named mailboxes for disputes, fraud and the processor portal without asking for an account (observed September 25, 2026).

US debit and ATM networks

The United States debit networks compete under one rule. Regulation II bars an issuer or a network from restricting a debit card to fewer than two unaffiliated networks, forbids a network from limiting an issuer's other contracts, and forbids inhibiting a merchant's routing choice, with card-not-present transactions covered since July 1, 2023 (Cornell LII, 12 CFR 235.7 · Federal Reserve Board finalizes updates). The interchange cap for issuers above 10 billion dollars in assets remains 21 cents plus five basis points, with a one cent fraud adjustment, and the 2023 proposal to lower it has no final rule as of September 2026 (eCFR Title 12 Part 235 · Federal Register API). The Federal Reserve's 2024 data give the networks their only comparable numbers: 37 cents average interchange on dual-message networks against 25 on single-message, and among the single-message networks PULSE and NYCE at 27 cents, Accel at 25, STAR, SHAZAM, AFFN and CULIANCE at 23 and Jeanie at 17 (Federal Reserve, Regulation II). The Board warns that these averages blend pricing programmes and do not say what an issuer earns on a given network (Federal Reserve, Regulation II). Everything else a partner would want, the switch fee, the membership fee, the rulebook, is unpublished at every one of them.

The site's own numbers disagree: nearly 70,000 surcharge-free ATMs on one page, nearly 40,000 on the MoneyPass page (Fiserv, Accel Network · Fiserv, MoneyPass).

AFFN

Armed Forces Financial Network · St. Petersburg, Florida · co-owned by two trade associations · military banks and credit unions, ATM and POS acceptance near bases

AFFN is a network owned by its members' associations, and it publishes the community and not the terms. Founded in 1985 at the Army's request, it is co-owned by the Association of Military Banks of America and the Defense Credit Union Council, and its site carries grant programmes, testimonials and executive names while the only rule document is the brand manual (AFFN, About Us · AFFN Matching Grant Program · AFFN Graphic Standards). Cirrus

Cirrus · Mastercard's global ATM brand · ATM operators and issuers through Mastercard

Cirrus is a cash-access brand without a public number. Mastercard defines it as its primary global cash-access solution, switches substantially all cross-border Cirrus transactions and earns fees on them, and excludes the brand from its reported volume (Mastercard 10-K 2025). ATM operators meet it through Mastercard's ATM network rules, and the surcharge non-discrimination rule that governs it is in the same litigation as Visa's (Mastercard 10-K 2025 · Visa 10-K 2025).

Interlink

Interlink · Visa's U.S. PIN debit network, operated as Interlink Network, Inc. · issuers and acquirers through Visa

Interlink is the back of a Visa debit card, with its own rules and its own schedule. The Department of Justice describes it as Visa's back-of-card network placed beside an unaffiliated network, and the complaint alleges Visa's issuer contracts discourage enabling card-present PINless, which keeps more transactions on the front of the card (Complaint, United States v. Visa). Visa publishes an Interlink interchange schedule and an Interlink rulebook, and licenses the marks as part of the Visa marks licence (Visa, Interlink Interchange Reimbursement Fees · Visa, Interlink Core Rules · Visa Core Rules).

OwnerVisa, through Interlink Network, Inc. with its own bylaws and core rules.(Visa rules · Visa Core Rules)
Regulation IIA single-message network. 27 cents average interchange across all 2024 transactions, 25 cents on covered ones.(Federal Reserve)
InterchangeExempt consumer retail 0.80 percent plus 15 cents, regulated 0.05 percent plus 21 cents, with the one cent fraud adjustment for certified issuers.(Visa Interlink schedule)
Market position, as allegedAll PIN networks together, Interlink and Maestro included, carry about 11 percent of U.S. debit transactions and 5 percent of card-not-present debit.(DOJ complaint)

Interlink has no partner surface of its own. It is a Visa sub-brand, and issuers, acquirers and developers meet it through Visa's programmes and portals.

Maestro

Maestro · Mastercard's PIN debit brand · issuers and merchants through Mastercard, retiring in Europe

Maestro is being retired in Europe and still counted in the United States. Since July 1, 2023 European issuers replace expired or lost Maestro cards with another product, and Mastercard's FY2025 filing still lists the brand without mentioning the phase-out (Mastercard, Blog from Valerie Nowak · Mastercard 10-K 2025). The Department of Justice describes Mastercard-branded U.S. debit cards as typically carrying Maestro plus an unaffiliated back-of-card network (Complaint, United States v. Visa). No public volume, card or transaction figure exists for the brand, since Mastercard excludes Maestro and Cirrus from its reported gross dollar volume (Mastercard 10-K 2025).

International schemes

Eight schemes outside the United States, in alphabetical order. Four of them are alliance partners of Discover: JCB, UnionPay, RuPay and Elo (Discover Global Network, Reach and Acceptance). Three publish more of their economics than any US network does: Interac its switch fees, eftpos its interchange and scheme fee changes, and Cartes Bancaires its interchange (Interac, Understanding Fees · Australian Payments Plus, AP+ lowers eftpos scheme fees · Cartes Bancaires, Les commissions interchange).

Cartes Bancaires

Groupement des Cartes Bancaires CB · Paris · an economic interest grouping of French banks · principal members in two colleges, acquirers and payment institutions, vendors through certification

CB is a members' grouping with published interchange and a certification arm. The interchange rates in force since January 2021 are public, 0.20 percent on debit and prepaid, 0.30 on credit and 0.90 on commercial, and the grouping says they pay for clearing, settlement, the payment guarantee and collective security (Cartes Bancaires, Les commissions interchange). Products reach the scheme through laboratory tests under the agrément programme run by its subsidiary PayCert, and acceptance providers through a two-tier labelisation (Cartes Bancaires, L’agrément CB · Paycert.eu · Cartes Bancaires, Labélisation CB). The live site answered this study's browser with a block page, and the REMPARTS portal did the same for plain fetches, so the public pages were read from archived copies (Page not found, walked · Browser Validation Page (Gcore)).

MembersPrincipal members in two colleges, partner banks and others. Adyen becomes a principal member and a direct STET participant from April 1, 2026.(CB, Adyen · Cartes Bancaires, Adyen devient membre principal de CB)
GovernanceA banks-and-industry advisory council twice a year and a commerce council with six merchant federations. A new chairman elected October 17, 2025.(CB · Cartes Bancaires, Gérald Grégoire, élu à l’unanimité, nouveau Président)

eftpos publishes the interchange schedule and lets the regulator set the frame. The schedule is public with current and legacy tabs by card and merchant category, strategic small-business rates fell to 2 cents in store and 3 cents online in December 2024, and issuer scheme fees were cut 22 percent in May 2025 (Australian Payments Plus, Interchange fees · Australian Payments Plus, Rollout of Merchant Choice Routing · Australian Payments Plus, AP+ lowers eftpos scheme fees). Elo

Elo Serviços · Brazil · owned by Banco do Brasil, Bradesco and Caixa · issuers, acquirers, sub-acquirers, wallets, processors, developers

Elo publishes a 694-page rulebook and lets anyone apply. The Regulamento dos Arranjos de Pagamento ELO, version 13.0 of May 11, 2026, defines every participant modality from post-paid issuer to sub-acquirer, gives participants 21 days to comment on changes, and states that any entity meeting its requirements may apply in writing and may appeal a refusal (Regulamento dos Arranjos de Pagamento ELO, Versão). Interchange is capped in the rulebook at 0.5 percent on debit and 0.7 on prepaid domestic purchases, while the fee annex describes every other mechanism and leaves the amounts to the partner portal (Regulamento dos Arranjos de Pagamento ELO, Versão).

Dev.Elo is a developer site with solutions, APIs, tutorials and a help centre, a self-service sign-up, a support mailbox, and a notice on the day that the portal was being modernised. The scheme's participant list is public, 352 institutions with their role, published as the Central Bank of Brazil requires (observed September 25, 2026 · ELO, walked).

Interac

Interac Corp. · Toronto · Canada's domestic debit and transfer network · financial institutions, acquirers, connection service providers, fintechs, developers

Interac publishes its wholesale prices to the tenth of a cent. The switch fee on a point-of-sale debit transaction is 1.3985 cents, rising to 1.4438 cents on November 1, 2026, and the e-Transfer connection fees are 50,000 dollars once and 20,000 a month for a direct participant (Interac, Understanding Fees). Interac sets interchange and does not receive it, and calls the switch fee cost recovery (Interac, Understanding Fees). The developer surface is by request per solution, immediate for identity products and conditional on an issuer relationship for payments (Interac, Support).

OwnerInterac Corp., reunited as one company in 2018, with more than 300 connected institutions.(Interac · Interac, Company Overview)
Volume, FY20257 billion Interac Debit, 1.6 billion e-Transfer and 544 million Interac Verified transactions, with 99.96 percent core availability.(Interac Year in Review)
ParticipationDirect and indirect connectors on the debit network. Three models on e-Transfer: direct, indirect through a connection service provider, or provider.(Interac · Interac e-Transfer participation)
InterchangeFlat fees by tier on contactless debit, from 2 cents on low-ticket categories. Interac Direct carries 55 to 70 basis points plus a 10 basis point brand fee.(Interac)
RulesA Competition Tribunal consent order bars restricting ATM surcharges. Point-of-sale surcharges are capped at 25 cents. A merchant complaint process answers in five business days.(Interac · Interac, FCAC Code of Conduct)

Interac's corporate site is for Canadians and Canadian businesses, and the partner material is a page on participant roles: direct and indirect connectors, issuers, acquirers, connection service providers and settlement agents, with a public acquirer list. The Innovation Hub is the developer surface, with Solutions, Community, Guides and Support, and its footnote sets the rule: access to specific products requires an existing relationship with an issuing financial institution. The hub's trend articles date from 2021 (observed September 25, 2026 · Innovation Hub, walked).
